Practical.title: SQL — Practical
Practical.body:
Q: What is the Difference between JDK, JRE, and JVM?
Ans • JDK is the development kit containing JRE and tools; JRE provides the libraries to run applications, and JVM is the engine that actually executes the bytecode.

Q: What is the purpose of the 'static' keyword?
Ans • The static keyword means the variable or method belongs to the class itself rather than an instance, allowing it to be accessed without creating an object.

Q: What is a Constructor in Java?
Ans • A constructor is a special method used to initialize objects; it has the same name as the class and no explicit return type.

Q: What is the 'final' keyword used for?
Ans • The final keyword is used to restrict the user: a final variable cannot be changed, a final method cannot be overridden, and a final class cannot be inherited.

Q: What is the difference between Array and ArrayList?
Ans • An Array is fixed in size, while an ArrayList is a dynamic collection that grows and shrinks automatically as elements are added or removed.

Q: What is Method Overloading vs Overriding?
Ans • Overloading happens when multiple methods have the same name but different parameters within the same class; Overriding occurs when a subclass provides a specific implementation of a method already defined in its parent class.
